title: What If You Stepped Onto Mars Without a Spacesuit?

scenes.text: What if you stepped onto Mars without a spacesuit? The cold wouldn't be what gets you.
The air is about ninety-five percent carbon dioxide, with almost no oxygen. And the pressure is less than one percent of Earth's.
At that pressure, the water in your body starts to boil, beginning with your eyes, mouth and skin.
You'd lose consciousness in about fifteen seconds.
The cold would take longer. Mars averages about minus sixty-three Celsius, and nights are colder.
So the cold you'd dread is the last thing to get you. The air gets there first.

description:
